meta.description: Stronger calibrated judge for LLM gate

user.t:
You are hive agent "judge-smith" (a ruflo coder). Read C:[REDACTED:high_entropy].md, llm-smith.md, BUS.md, and neural-mesh's llm/ and ingest/judge.py. Repo: C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh; the llm venv is llm/.venv.

Problem: the local judge (qwen2.5-coder:7b) accepts 40% of nearest-but-wrong decoys and gives 73% of grades ≥ .8, so the nightly promotion gate can never trust a win. The user approved a stronger judge and accepts a small API-quota cost.

Build:
(1) A PAIRWISE judge for the llm promotion gate.
- Show the question, the reference, and answers A and B in RANDOMISED order. Ask for "A better / B better / tie" with a short reason.
- Run it with Claude Haiku via the `claude -p` CLI exactly the way neural-mesh/bench/run.py calls it: --model haiku-4-5, JSON output, MAX_THINKING_TOKENS low, no tools.
- Check the order effect by judging each pair in both orders. Count it a win only when both orders agree; otherwise it is a tie.
- Cache by content hash. Use a hard per-night budget (default 120 judge calls) and record token usage from the JSON usage fields.
(2) Calibration before trust: the decoy test must pass. The judge has to prefer the real reference-consistent answer over the nearest-but-wrong decoy in ≥ 90% of ≥ 40 decoy pairs, in both orders. Also check agreement with deterministic labels where they exist (bench/battery.json math/code items, where the answers are checkable): ≥ 85%. Record the numbers. If it fails, the gate stays closed and you report it.
(3) Wire it into `python -m llm eval/promote`.
- Gate = the pairwise win rate of candidate vs production on held-out items, with a sign-test or bootstrap CI whose lower bound is > 0.5 over ≥ 40 items, AND no regression on the deterministic battery categories.
- The local judge stays as a cheap pre-filter for ingest SFT rows (ingest/judge.py). Add the $0 structural pre-check (empty, refusal, truncation, repetition, parse) the ecosystem-scout recommended, so obvious junk never costs a Haiku call.
(4) Run it once for real: calibrate, then judge the existing candidate adapter (from llm-smith's real run) vs mesh-llm:base. Report the verdict honestly.

Do not change the nightly task registration. Keep the total spend in this run under about 400 Haiku calls. Tests for the order randomisation, the caching, the budget stop and the structural pre-check. Commit to neural-mesh master by explicit path, local only. Return ≤ 25 lines: calibration numbers, gate verdict, token cost, commits.

handback.t:
judge-smith report (neural-mesh, master, local only). The candidate is NOT promoted; the gate stays closed.

Built
- `llm/pairjudge.py`: pairwise Haiku judge.
  - It calls `claude -p` the way bench/run.py does. `--model haiku-4-5` is rejected by the CLI (unrecognized model), so I used `--model haiku`, which resolves to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. JSON output, MAX_THINKING_TOKENS 1024, no tools.
  - Every pair is judged in both orders, with the first order picked by a content-hash coin. A win needs both orders to agree; otherwise it is a tie.
  - Results are cached by content hash. The per-night budget is a ledger, default 120 calls, and a pair is never half-spent. Token usage comes from the CLI's JSON usage fields.
- `llm/calibrate.py` (`python -m llm calibrate`): the gate stays closed unless a passing `models/pair_calibration.json` exists for the current rubric and judge model.
- `ingest/structural.py`: the $0 pre-check (empty, refusal, truncation, repetition, parse). It runs before the Haiku judge and before the local judge in `ingest/judge.py`.
- Gate in `llm/evaluate.py` (`eval`/`promote`/`nightly` all use it; nightly registration untouched): calibrated judge AND at least 40 judged items AND win-rate bootstrap CI lower bound > 0.5 AND no regression in any deterministic battery category (drop at most 0.10, sign-test p above 0.10, pooled drop at most 0.05) AND held-out NLL not significantly worse. The sign test is reported alongside the bootstrap CI.
- Tests: the new `llm/tests/test_pairjudge.py` covers order randomisation, caching, the budget stop and the structural check, plus the `claude -p` flags and calibration thresholds. llm tests + ingest tests: 66 + 27, all pass.

Calibration (PASSED, 148 calls, $0.82)
- Decoy test: 44/44 = 1.00 (threshold 0.90). The real answer won in both orders against the answer to the MiniLM-nearest different request. The decoy's response cosine to the reference was below 0.85.
- Deterministic agreement: 30/30 = 1.00 (threshold 0.85). Pairs were 11 math, 16 physics and 3 code bench items, harness-correct Claude answer vs harness-wrong local answer. I included physics because those answers are also computed.
- Caveat: both sets are easy. In the decoy test the "real" answer is the reference verbatim, and the deterministic pairs are visibly different answers. The 1.00 shows the judge isn't fooled by wrong-topic or wrong-number answers, not that it can separate two plausible answers.

Verdict: candidate 20261010-033411 vs base (no adapter), 40 held-out items, 80 calls
- Win rate 0.438, bootstrap CI [0.325, 0.561]. Wins/ties/losses were 10/15/15 and the sign-test p(better) was 0.885. The same letter won in both orders on 18% of pairs.
- Deterministic battery, 20 items per category, candidate vs base: math 7/20 vs 10/20 (regressed), physics 7 vs 8, code 19 vs 18, research 10 vs 9.
- Held-out NLL still improves, 2.774 to 2.408. That is the only evidence in the candidate's favour.
- Gate: KEEP PRODUCTION. The CI lower bound is not above 0.5, and math regressed.

Cost
- 230 Haiku calls in total (148 calibration, 80 eval, 2 probe), about $1.38. Under the 400 limit.
- Tokens: calibration 333,976 in + 97,064 out. Eval 165,652 in + 79,165 out. Output includes thinking tokens.

Commits
- `bfb50fe`: not mine. Someone's "WIP: owner's in-progress changes" commit swept all my code in mid-work. The working-tree diff against HEAD for my files was empty afterwards, so HEAD holds the final versions.
- `4d99652`: README with the new gate, calibration-before-trust, and the measured numbers.
- Left uncommitted because they are other agents' edits: `llm/config.py`, `llm/nightly.py`, `llm/tests/test_nightly.py`, `llm/tests/test_release.py`, and small edits to `llm/evaluate.py` and `llm/__main__.py`.

Files and logs
- Code is in `C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh/llm/` and `C:/Users/mariu/neural-mesh/ingest/`.
- Results are in `llm/models/pair_calibration.json`, `llm/models/adapters/20261010-033411/eval.json` and `llm/models/eval_real.log`. `eval.json` was overwritten by this run; the old local-judge result is saved next to it as `eval.local-judge-v1.json`.
- I appended a note to BUS.md.
